claim.statement: Kimera-SWM's Walker M3 selective-halt mode functions as a substrate-native linguistic-discontinuity detector. When activated, it emits a single concept that captures the rhetorical center of who-just-spoke or what-just-changed, then halts.
claim.operationalization: Out of 515 Takwin cycles on pg100.txt prose, 10 produced 'selective' resolution (the Walker's M3 mode). Each is inspected against linguistic-discontinuity markers: (a) speaker-switch (CAPS:NAME at paragraph start) or (b) meta-textual self-reference. Heuristic detector + manual verification.
claim.h0: Selective halts are random with respect to linguistic discontinuities (~50%)
claim.h1: Selective halts cluster on linguistic discontinuities

preregistration.analysis_plan: Wilson interval + exact binomial vs 50% null. n=10 small; finding flagged for replication at n=30+.

verdict.reasoning: 9 of 10 selective halts landed on linguistic discontinuities (8 by heuristic, +1 from manual verification of FIRST LORD speaker switch). Wilson 95% CI [0.60, 0.98]; exact binomial 2-sided p vs 50% null = 0.0215. Significant at α=0.05. Single-concept emissions are speaker thematic-fingerprints (PAROLLES → regiment; HELENA → prescriptions; KING → florentines) or rhetorical pivots (CLOWN → whither; FIRST LORD → younger).
